contents.reason: The pair's finite check is the sl3 adjoint module, which already exercises a two-term Kostant partition and the sl3 dot action. An sp4 computation would need a separate sp4 root-system data package that this pair does not scaffold, and the design's B inventory does not include it.

contents.name: §26.5 Weyl dimension formula: specialization h = 2t h_ρ, factorization of the numerator and the limit t → 0 (Prop. 26.8)
contents.proof_mapping: evaluated denominator identity, quotient identity and limit; thm-weyl-dimension-formula is the assembled statement

contents.name: §26.5 principal grading by the eigenvalues of 2h_ρ and its Poincaré-polynomial product formula
contents.reason: The principal sl2 grading and its Poincare polynomial are not consumed by any item of this pair; only the t → 0 limit of the character quotient is used, so building the grading would add a parallel inventory with no proof consumer.

contents.name: §26.4, printed p. 141, proof of Theorem 26.4: a dominant subweight $\mu=\lambda+\rho-\beta$ with $\beta\in Q^+\setminus\{0\}$ satisfies $|\mu|^2<|\lambda+\rho|^2$ via $2(\lambda+\rho,\beta)-|\beta|^2>(\lambda+\rho-\beta,\beta)\ge0$
contents.proof_mapping: The dominant-weight case of the lemma is exactly this step; the reduction of an arbitrary weight to its dominant conjugate uses the local $\rho-w\rho$ lemma with the published orbit and W-invariance items.

contents.name: §26.2, printed p. 139: $s_i$ permutes the positive roots other than $\alpha_i$ and sends $\alpha_i$ to $-\alpha_i$; the sign character $(-1)^{\ell(w)}=\det(w|_{\mathfrak h})$
contents.proof_mapping: Simple-reflection computation $2s_i\rho=2\rho-2\alpha_i$, giving $\langle\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=1$ and $s_i\rho=\rho-\alpha_i$, the induction step for $\rho-w\rho$.
